output.title: When spot checks stop finding the problem
output.body:
This is for the owner of a small business who is still doing important checks by hand. Spot checks work until they stop telling you anything useful: the same errors keep coming back, or new ones slip through between reviews. Then the real question is not “should I inspect more?” It is “which part of this check can be made reliable, and which part must stay human?”

A good candidate is a repeatable document or data review with clear rules. Think invoice amounts against an expected limit, customer replies against a simple FAQ list, or recurring form fields that should match a known pattern. That is where AI can help with flagging and routing. It should not be used to make the final call on money movement or other high-risk decisions; that boundary stays with the owner.

The practical next step is to name one workflow and one failure point. Which check fails most often, and what exactly goes wrong? That gives you a bounded decision: keep the human approval where it belongs, and only automate the repetitive part that can be checked against rules. Small distinction, big difference.
